Anna Kim: Quick sync / apples-to-apples loadbench comparing synthetic traffic vs replayed prod traces. Need a short checklist + gotchas before I run. :eyes:
Sam Ortiz: First things first: tokenizer + role framing must match. Synthetic runs often forget system messages or role separators.
Leo Chen: Also ensure KV-cache warmup parity. Replay traces include long prefixes that prime KV; synthetic payloads often skip that and skew tail latency.
Maya Patel: Strongly recommend stratified sampling by token-length cohorts (short/medium/long). Uniform sampling hides edge cases.
Anna Kim: Draft checklist:
- Tokenizer parity (vocab, casing, special tokens)
- Keep role markers and system messages counts
- Anonymize but preserve token lengths & punctuation
- Cohort stratification and per-cohort sizes
- Deterministic sampler seed
- Option to pin kernel selection for determinism
- Match KV prewarm policy
- Same batching config (max_batch, max_delay_ms)
- Collect per-token latency + top-k logits for divergence checks
Sam Ortiz: Can we script it? I want a one-liner that emits a deterministic replay slice and runs both benches.
Anna Kim: Yes, helper I use:
```bash
./tools/replay_slice \  --trace s3:\/\/prod-traces\/trace-2026-02.gz \  --anonymize hash-uid --preserve-token-lengths \  --cohorts short,medium,long --cohort-size 2000 \  --seed 1729 \  --pin-kernel matmul_v2 \  --batch 4 --max-delay-ms 20 \  --out /tmp/replay_slice.json
# run harness (replay)
./tools/run_harness --input /tmp/replay_slice.json --mode replay --profile /tmp/perf_replay.out
# run harness (synthetic with shapes from slice)
./tools/run_harness --input /tmp/replay_slice.json --mode synthetic --profile /tmp/perf_synth.out
```
Leo Chen: Note: --pin-kernel is crucial when kernel selection is heuristic/timing-dependent. If we don't pin, tiny timing diffs can change kernel choice and break apples->apples.
Maya Patel: For anonymization: hash UIDs and scrub PII but preserve token-count and role markers. Replace URLs/emails with single tokens like [URL] so tokenization length stays the same.
Sam Ortiz: Define parity criteria? Bitwise equality is unrealistic. My proposal:
- Throughput delta < 3%
- p90 latency delta < 5%
- Top-10 logits L2 < 0.08 (or configurable)
- KS test overlap on token latency distribution > 0.9
Anna Kim: Add kernel-selection logs and env snapshot to artifacts (e.g., KERNEL_PICK=1, KERNEL_BLACKLIST) so we can verify same kernel path.
infra-bot: bench job started on bench-cluster-7, run id 2026-03-21-42
Leo Chen: If replay shows regression but synthetic doesn't, check data-shape mismatches first: missing prefixes, role markup, KV priming, or different batch occupancy histograms.
Maya Patel: Example symptom we saw: throughput matched but p95 was +30% on replay; root cause was synthetic omitted a prefix-squash step -> different KV hit behavior.
Sam Ortiz: Profiling snippet we compare across runs (high-level):
```text
50% runtime_kernel_dispatch
12% kv_cache_lookup
8% attention_matmul
5% tokenizer_normalize
```
Anna Kim: Bench report should include: kernel time breakdown, batch occupancy histogram, KV hit/miss rates, per-token latency histograms, and logits divergence summary.
Maya Patel: On sampling: use stratified reservoir sampling with a fixed seed: sample N per cohort by hash(uid,seed) so slices are deterministic and repeatable.
Leo Chen: Test multiple arrival shapes: steady, ramp, spike, and Poisson-like noisy arrivals. Production burstiness often triggers different kernel paths. Synthetic tools default to constant inter-arrival which masks that.
Anna Kim: Run plan:
1) Emit deterministic, anonymized replay slice with cohorts
2) Run replay harness (pin kernel, profile)
3) Run synthetic harness using shapes from slice
4) Gather metrics, run parity checks
5) If any metric exceeds thresholds, open postmortem with artifacts
Sam Ortiz: Can we add nightly CI that runs this on bench infra and files tickets automatically if thresholds are crossed?
Maya Patel: I'll draft a runbook + GH issue template that includes checklist and required logs/artifacts.
Anna Kim: Kicking off first full run now. DM me if you want the slice.
infra-bot: Bench run completed. run id 2026-03-21-42. Summary: replay throughput 12.1k tpm, synthetic 12.4k tpm (delta -2.4%). p95 replay 210ms vs synthetic 198ms -> p95 delta +6.1% (exceeds threshold). Artifacts: s3://bench/artifacts/2026-03-21-42/
Sam Ortiz: p95 delta >5% / tagging @eng-runtime for investigation. :mag:
Leo Chen: I'll pull perf_replay.out and compare kernel call counts and KV hit rates now.
Maya Patel: I'll produce cohort histograms and token-length distributions.
Anna Kim: Thanks everyone. Will post root cause once I have diffs. :+1:
